correctness.rationale: A full SOR sweep gives an explicit 2x2 residual matrix R. The determinant of I-R^T R factors into two scalar factors; one stays positive throughout 0<omega<2, so the sign change is exactly at omega_E=2s/(1+s-s^2). The remaining principal minor is nonnegative throughout the claimed safe interval. The classical spectral-radius optimum is recovered independently from the characteristic discriminant of the SOR error matrix, and comparing the two exact parameters gives s^2>=1/2, equivalently kappa<=3+2sqrt(2). The rational kappa=9 witness is replayed by the packaged checker.

A later full SOR-type parameter-optimization paper likewise centers on spectral radii and contains no residual-norm occurrence in the accessible text. Targeted searches did not locate the exact residual-safe ceiling or the 3+2sqrt(2) crossover between asymptotic optimality and one-sweep residual monotonicity.

The theorem is restricted to the equal-diagonal Jacobi-scaled family; a robust all-2x2 SPD SOR frontier could differ.

value.rationale: SOR is classically tuned by asymptotic spectral radius, while residual norm is a standard practical stopping diagnostic. The theorem identifies exactly when these two objectives first conflict on the canonical two-coordinate SPD model and gives a closed-form safe relaxation ceiling, a sharp condition-number crossover, and a simple exact residual spike. This is a motivated transient-versus-asymptotic distinction rather than a routine parameter substitution.
